Short answer: it's not off-limits at 16, but a true one-rep max isn't where I'd start. Teens can lift heavy safely when technique is solid and someone qualified is watching, ideally a coach or a spotter who knows what they're doing, with a proper warm-up and sensible jumps in weight.

For most people your age I'd rather you build a heavy set of 3 to 5 reps with clean form. That tells us nearly as much about your strength, carries less risk, and doesn't leave you grinding a rep with ugly technique. If you do want to test a max down the road, do it on a lift you know well, with spotters or safeties set, and stop the moment form breaks.

If you have any health concerns or a medical condition, check with your doctor before testing anything heavy. Want me to look at where your main lifts are sitting right now so we can pick a good heavy set to work toward?
